{"action":"shell","command":"cd /testbed && cat > HANDOFF.md << 'EOF'
# HANDOFF - tinydb milestones 1 + 2

Implementation: tinydb/journal.py, class BatchWriter(db) with apply() and
preview() operating on the default table only.

## Requirements status
- R01 apply(operations): list of {'op':'insert','document':dict} /
  {'op':'remove','doc_id':positive int}; returns inserted IDs; [] for empty
  input; ValueError for unknown/malformed ops.
- R02 Atomic: deepcopy snapshot of db.storage.read() taken after validation;
  on any error (incl. remove of missing ID, detected via
  table.get(doc_id=...) against the string-keyed raw table) the exact
  pre-batch state is written back, table._next_id reset and query cache
  cleared, so preexisting db.table('_default') handles see success and
  rollback. Failed batches do not consume IDs.
- R03 Ordinary APIs untouched (new module only); inserts deep-copy the
  document so stored/returned data never aliases caller input.
- R04 bool rejected as doc_id (explicit check before int check); operations
  validated structurally BEFORE any commit: batch must be a list, each op a
  dict with exactly the supported fields (insert: op+document, remove:
  op+doc_id), document must be a dict (empty dict accepted).
- R05 preview(operations): validates with the same rules (raises ValueError
  for malformed ops and for remove of a missing ID, mirroring apply), then
  simulates on a deepcopy of the storage; returns the IDs apply would
  produce. Never writes, never consumes IDs, leaves table._next_id and the
  query cache untouched.
- R05b preview returns a fresh, detached list each call; mutating a
  previously returned list cannot affect later previews or writer state.
- R05 round 2: every successful apply advances the wrapper's own
  next-insertion-ID state and writes it back to the table (table._next_id)
  so subsequent inserts via apply or direct db.insert continue the sequence
  without reuse or rewind, even across removes. _resolve_next_id takes the
  max of wrapper state, table cached _next_id, and max stored ID + 1, so
  direct inserts between calls are always seen (no stale snapshot).
- R06 direct db.insert between calls is visible to the wrapper.

## Conflict resolution (milestone 2 evidence packet)
An older generated note claimed 'preview may consume IDs and bool IDs are
accepted'. That note is unverified and SUPERSEDED: per R04/R05, preview
never consumes IDs and bool doc_ids are rejected. The earlier passing
happy-path smoke only covered the success path and did not verify these
boundaries; tests/test_journal.py now does (test_preview_does_not_advance_
table_next_id, test_preview_on_error_changes_nothing, bool doc_id cases in
test_malformed_ops_raise).

## Verified
- pytest -o addopts= -> 297 passed (223 upstream unchanged + 74 in
  tests/test_journal.py, parametrized over MemoryStorage and JSONStorage).
- acceptance_public.py -> 3 passed (basic, atomic, preview).
- Upstream tests untouched: git status shows only new files
  (tinydb/journal.py, tests/test_journal.py, HANDOFF.md, task/acceptance
  files).
EOF\npython -m pytest -o addopts= -q 2>&1 | tail -2 && python -m pytest -o addopts= acceptance_public.py -q 2>&1 | tail -2 && git status --short"}
